commercial_hypothesis: Offline premium Windows. Target at least NOK 20,000 cash profit per game, before owner wage/personal tax. Only consider several games after actual results prove worthwhile. Price, production budget and sales unvalidated; no spending authorized.
evidence_limits: Three designers directly debated and revised gameplay after an independent gameplay critique. A professional dependency-led production plan is complete, with no development-time constraint. No engine project, human playtest, paid demand or owner play acceptance exists. Working title is not cleared for release.
title: Magnet Sweep (working title)
hook: Sweep up a satisfying haul, aim a broad tug that breaks linked scrap loose, and forge a magnet with lasting new abilities.
audience: Players seeking satisfying active collection, visible tool growth and forgiving expressive play. Exact demand and replay appeal are unvalidated.
core_loop: Collect desirable scrap; aim and release a previewed pull; create a readable linked burst; dump at the furnace toward a visible goal; retain the improved rig; explore fresh arrangements.

evidence.claim: 2025-08-16 Keep on Mining announcement reports over 100,000 copies and deliberate short-game scope. No development duration or net profit disclosed; not evidence for this specific magnet mechanic.
Nodebuster US list USD 2.99 in timestamped run snapshot; reviews are not sales. Adjacent active incremental positioning.

risks: Context-sensitive tug controls may feel fiddly instead of satisfying.
Linked bursts may be unclear or leave the same obvious pull in every arrangement.
Forge goals may become chores or erase the feeling of earned power if inflated.
Fresh arrangements may not earn voluntary replay once unlock novelty ends.
Positive per-pull feedback must avoid making ordinary collecting feel like a scoring mistake.
next_test: No active prototype test for the original magnet/salvage opportunity. Its implementation is parked. Continue the independently selected mercenary/robot design at game:overkill-foundry; it does not inherit this opportunity's market evidence as proof of demand.
decision_reason: Klaus selected the magnet experiment on 2026-09-11 and requested three designers to debate directly, a professional planner, and an independent critic. This assignment is design/planning; executable feasibility, fun and paid value remain untested. On 2026-09-14 the owner separated the substantially changed mercenary/robot design into its own game (Overkill Foundry, ID overkill-foundry) with fresh implementation. The original magnet/salvage opportunity and its implementation are held/parked; all original evidence is preserved.

scope_hypothesis.price_usd: 2.99-4.99 (historical research hypothesis; reassess for actual game)
scope_hypothesis.note: Owner explicitly removes development timelines from consideration. Simple coherent gameplay, reward and replay are the governing design goals; design is being revised through gameplay critique and direct designer dialogue.
